articles.title: Supermassive black hole winds are 100 times more powerful than scientists thought
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered that winds from a supermassive black hole are about 100 times more powerful than previously thought. XRISM observations showed the resulting turbulence spreading roughly 300,000 light-years, extending far beyond the black hole’s host galaxy. The energy involved rivals several billion supernova explosions, revealing just how dramatically black holes can influence the space around them.
articles.content:
Supermassive black holes may have a much larger influence on their surroundings than scientists previously realized. New observations suggest that winds driven by these enormous objects can carry energy across roughly 300,000 light-years, reaching far beyond the galaxies that host them.

Researchers found that the energy associated with these winds is about 100 times greater than earlier estimates, revealing that black holes can affect vast regions of space on a truly enormous scale.

"Black holes are largely known for sucking matter in, but they also eject gas in the form of powerful winds," says Satoshi Yamada, Assistant Professor at Tohoku University's Frontier Institute for Interdisciplinary Sciences (FRIS). "These winds were thought to be contained within the galaxy, but our study revealed that the force is immensely more powerful than previously understood."

XRISM Takes a Closer Look at a Distant Quasar

Yamada and his colleagues, including researchers from Kanazawa University and Tokyo Metropolitan University, among others, used the X ray astronomy satellite XRISM to study the quasar H1821+643. The object lies in the constellation Draco, about 3.4 billion light-years from Earth.

Quasars are exceptionally bright cosmic objects powered by supermassive black holes that are actively consuming gas. As material falls toward the black hole, tremendous amounts of energy can be released, making quasars visible across immense distances.

The rapidly growing black hole at the center of H1821+643 sits within a galaxy cluster. There, it stirs the surrounding hot gas, which gives off X-rays. To measure how that gas was moving, the researchers analyzed emission lines produced by iron ions.

Black Hole Turbulence Reaches Far Beyond the Galaxy

XRISM's high-precision measurements showed that the extremely hot gas around the black hole is far from motionless. Instead, turbulence causes it to spread violently across a broad region.

The team also found that this gas flow extends beyond the black hole's host galaxy, reaching distances of about 300,000 light-years. Even more striking, the energy contained in the turbulence was approximately 100 times greater than previous estimates.

That amount of energy is comparable to the output of several billion supernova explosions, the powerful blasts produced when certain stars reach the ends of their lives.

"For the first time, we have shown that black holes influence the broader cosmic environment through a shock wave of astonishing power," adds Yamada. "Black holes are key drivers of gas flows and motion in space, transporting vast amounts of energy to different regions of the cosmos."

A Bigger Role for Black Holes in the Cosmos

The findings suggest that supermassive black holes do more than consume nearby matter. They can also send energy and gas far into surrounding space, potentially helping shape the environments around galaxies and galaxy clusters.

Details of the research were published in the journal Nature Astronomy.

Future observations are expected to provide a clearer picture of how black holes affect their surroundings and how matter and elements move through different regions of the cosmos.

articles.personality_title: Supermassive black hole winds are 100 times stronger than thought
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Scientists have studied supermassive black holes, which are huge objects in space that can pull in gas and matter. These black holes also blow out winds, but until now, their full strength and reach were not well known.

**What happened** – Using a special X-ray satellite called XRISM, researchers looked at a quasar named H1821+643, located 3.4 billion light-years away. They found that the winds from its supermassive black hole spread turbulence across 300,000 light-years, much farther than expected. The energy in these winds is about 100 times greater than earlier estimates.

**Impact** – This discovery shows that black holes don’t just pull things in; they also send powerful energy and gas far into space. The energy released by these winds is like billions of supernova explosions combined. This means black holes can shape the space around them on a much larger scale than scientists thought before.

**What's next step** – Scientists will continue to study black holes with XRISM and other tools to learn more about how these winds move gas and elements through space. This will help us better understand how galaxies and galaxy clusters change over time.

**One-sentence takeaway** – New observations reveal that supermassive black hole winds are far stronger and reach much farther into space than previously believed, affecting entire cosmic neighborhoods.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les vents des trous noirs supermassifs sont 100 fois plus puissants que prévu
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Les scientifiques étudient les trous noirs supermassifs, d’énormes objets dans l’espace qui attirent gaz et matière. Ces trous noirs émettent aussi des vents, mais leur force et leur portée exactes étaient jusqu’ici mal connues.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Grâce au satellite à rayons X XRISM, des chercheurs ont observé un quasar nommé H1821+643, situé à 3,4 milliards d’années-lumière. Ils ont découvert que les vents de son trou noir supermassif provoquent des turbulences sur 300 000 années-lumière, bien plus loin qu’attendu. L’énergie de ces vents est environ 100 fois plus grande que les estimations précédentes.

**Impact** – Cette découverte montre que les trous noirs n’aspirent pas seulement la matière, mais envoient aussi de l’énergie et du gaz puissants très loin dans l’espace. L’énergie libérée équivaut à plusieurs milliards d’explosions de supernova. Cela signifie que les trous noirs peuvent influencer beaucoup plus largement leur environnement cosmique que ce que l’on pensait.

**Prochaines étapes** – Les scientifiques continueront d’étudier les trous noirs avec XRISM et d’autres instruments pour mieux comprendre comment ces vents déplacent gaz et éléments dans l’espace. Cela aidera à mieux saisir l’évolution des galaxies et des amas de galaxies.

**Résumé en une phrase** – De nouvelles observations montrent que les vents des trous noirs supermassifs sont bien plus puissants et étendus que prévu, affectant des régions entières de l’univers.
articles.personality_title_es: Los vientos de los agujeros negros supermasivos son 100 veces más fuertes de lo pensado
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Los científicos han estudiado los agujeros negros supermasivos, enormes objetos en el espacio que atraen gas y materia. Estos agujeros negros también expulsan vientos, pero hasta ahora no se conocía su verdadera fuerza y alcance.

**Qué pasó** – Usando un satélite especial de rayos X llamado XRISM, los investigadores observaron un quasar llamado H1821+643, a 3.4 mil millones de años luz. Descubrieron que los vientos de su agujero negro supermasivo causan turbulencia que se extiende hasta 300,000 años luz, mucho más lejos de lo esperado. La energía en estos vientos es unas 100 veces mayor que las estimaciones anteriores.

**Impacto** – Este descubrimiento muestra que los agujeros negros no solo atraen materia, sino que también envían energía y gas muy poderosos a grandes distancias en el espacio. La energía liberada es como la de miles de millones de explosiones de supernova. Esto significa que los agujeros negros pueden influir en el espacio a su alrededor en una escala mucho mayor de lo que se creía.

**Próximo paso** – Los científicos seguirán estudiando los agujeros negros con XRISM y otras herramientas para entender mejor cómo estos vientos mueven gas y elementos en el espacio. Esto ayudará a comprender cómo cambian las galaxias y los cúmulos de galaxias con el tiempo.

**Una frase clave** – Nuevas observaciones revelan que los vientos de los agujeros negros supermasivos son mucho más fuertes y se extienden mucho más lejos de lo que se pensaba, afectando vecindarios cósmicos enteros.
